chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you pray behind an Imam whom one does not follow (in all matters), then recite behind him, whether you hear his recitation or do not hear it."

key_terms.إِمَامٍ لاَ يُقْتَدَى بِهِ: An Imam whom one does not follow (in all matters of jurisprudence or qualification)

ai.seo_question: Do I need to recite Surah al-Fatihah when praying behind an Imam who is not fully qualified?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the status of the follower (muqtadi) when praying behind an Imam who is not fully qualified (la yuqtada bihi), such as a follower of another school or a less learned Imam. It establishes that the follower must independently recite Surah al-Fatihah behind such an Imam, a ruling that holds true whether the follower can hear the Imam’s recitation or not, emphasizing the necessity of personal recitation in this specific context. This distinction highlights the Shia view that the validity of the prayer in such cases relies on the follower's own recitation rather than mere imitation of the Imam's recitation.
